candidate_abstract: Existing ASR training objectives allow a model to explore multiple temporal alignments between input features and output labels. candidate_title: LINK: Adaptive Modality Interaction for Audio-Visual Video Parsing
candidate_abstract: Audio-visual video parsing combines weakly labelled video classification with identifying the temporal limits of events that are visible, audible, or both. Methods that fail to account for misalignment between modalities can introduce additional noise during their interaction. Learning Interaction for Non-aligned Knowledge (LINK) is designed to balance modality contributions by dynamically adjusting their inputs during event prediction. The method also uses pseudo-label semantics as prior knowledge to mitigate noise from other modalities. Experiments on the LLP dataset show that LINK outperforms existing methods.

candidate_title: Bosonic Random Walk Networks for Graph Learning
candidate_abstract: Graph neural networks have advanced learning on graph-structured data by diffusing information between nodes while encoding graph structure. Alongside recent progress in quantum computing, this work investigates multi-particle quantum walks for spreading information across graphs. The model learns the operators that control the dynamics of quantum random walkers on the graph. Its effectiveness is demonstrated on classification and regression tasks.
